It’s been about two months now where things just feel… wrong, like something’s coming. I know this’ll sound odd, but I keep getting this feeling that everything is winding down, like the whole world’s about to collapse. Not in a metaphorical way—more like I’m convinced some massive disaster is right around the corner, like there’s no point planning anything long term because it’s already over, we just haven’t caught up to it yet.

At work, I’m supposed to be scanning crowds, watching exits, staying sharp. Lately I’ve been seeing things that aren’t there—people standing in doorways, shadows moving against walls, sometimes whole figures in the corner of my eye. I’ll turn to confront them and they’re just… gone. It throws me off, makes me second-guess what I’m seeing, which is dangerous in my line of work.

On top of that, I’ve had stretches where I’m running on very little sleep but still feel wired, talking faster than usual, taking on extra shifts like I’m invincible. Then other times, the dread about everything ending hits me harder again. I can’t really tell how all of this fits together, but it’s been messing with my job and my head.
D005-D010_h001.question_a:

Pretty much every day, I’m convinced something catastrophic is about to happen, like the whole world is about to just…stop existing. It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels like a fact. I’ll be standing outside a client’s car and suddenly “know” that none of this is real and everything’s about to be wiped out.

I also keep seeing things that aren’t there. Dark figures in the corners, people walking past me who vanish when I look twice, the sky kind of “cracking” like broken glass. This happens whether I’m at work, at home, calm, or stressed—there’s no break from it.

On top of that, there was about a week where I barely slept, felt wired, talking faster, thinking I could take on any job, even joked about starting my own agency. But that high, energetic feeling faded. The strange beliefs and seeing things never stopped; they’ve just kept going straight through, with or without that brief “amped-up” period.
D005-D010_h001.question_b:

I’ve been taking extra shifts, convinced I can handle anything, even talking about starting my own security company and “rebuilding the world” after what’s coming.

When I’m in that state, I see shadows and figures out of the corner of my eye—people standing in doorways or in the street—and when I look straight at them, they’re gone. Sometimes I see the sky crack or buildings crumbling, like a preview of the end.

It started with this huge burst of energy. I barely sleep—maybe two, three hours—but I still feel wired, like my brain is going faster than my hands can sketch. I talk nonstop at work, jump from one design idea to another, start five projects and don’t finish any. I’ve been spending way too much on materials and furniture “for my future studio,” even though my salary doesn’t cover it. I feel ridiculously confident, like I’m destined to be famous in the field.

Around the same time, I became convinced that a well‑known architect I follow online is secretly in love with me. I’m sure he’s sending me messages through his posts, even though we’ve never met. Sometimes I suddenly taste things—like metallic blood or really sweet syrup—out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating. My coworkers say I’ve been acting “goofy,” making silly jokes in client meetings, giggling at nothing, even spinning in the office chair when everyone’s being serious.

All of this—the beliefs, the weird tastes, the silly behavior—only happens during this revved‑up, high period. When my mood briefly dipped back to normal for a week, those things completely went away.

I’ve been sailing most of my life, so I’m used to odd things at sea, but this is different. For about three months now I’ve had this fixed idea that people are keeping tabs on me. When I’m in port, I’m sure the harbor office and even some of my own crew are passing reports about me, like I’m under some kind of watch. At home, I’ll catch myself checking the windows, feeling like there’s someone in a car outside with binoculars, even though my wife says there’s nothing there.

I also get these strange sensations on my skin, like something crawling along my arms or the back of my neck, almost like a rope brushing me, but when I look there’s nothing. It happens both on the ship and at home.

My mood’s been all over the place. Some days I feel wired and driven, barely sleeping and talking too fast, making grand plans for new routes and investments. Other days I just shut down and don’t answer when my wife or crew talk to me or ask me to do something; I just… dig my heels in, almost on purpose, but I can’t explain why.
D005-D010_h024.question_a:

On the bridge I’m constantly checking the radar and cameras, convinced there’s some group tracking me, maybe through the ship’s systems or my phone. Even at home, I think there are people parked outside, keeping tabs on me and my wife. My crew tells me it’s nothing, but I *know* they’re monitoring me.

I also keep feeling things crawling or moving on my skin, like someone’s brushing past me or tapping my shoulder, but when I look, there’s nothing there. It happens in my bunk, at the dinner table, even during drills. It makes me jumpy and on edge.

My wife says I’ve become hard to deal with. Sometimes, when she or the officers ask me to do something simple—take my meds, sign a form, answer a question—I just freeze or stubbornly won’t respond, even when I know I should.

A few weeks back I had a short spell where I barely slept, talked a lot, felt oddly energized and overconfident about handling any voyage—but these ideas of being watched and the strange skin sensations have been there before, during, and after that, without letting up.

I guess this all really started about three months ago. I’ve been getting this…fixed idea that there’s something seriously wrong inside my chest or my head, like my organs are rotting or wired wrong. I’ve had checkups, bloodwork, scans, and they keep telling me everything’s fine, but it doesn’t feel fine. I keep pressing on my ribs or my neck at work, kind of checking over and over without realizing I’m doing it, and my team has started to notice.

Around the same time, I began smelling this faint, burnt‑metal or chemical odor that no one else seems to notice. It’ll hit me in the warehouse, in the car, sometimes even in bed at night. I’ll ask my wife if she smells it, and she just looks confused.

My sleep’s been all over the place lately. Some weeks I’m wired and barely sleep, but I’m still going full throttle at work, talking fast, taking on extra projects, like my mind is revved up. Other times I crash and feel more flat, but the worry about my body and those weird smells doesn’t really go away in either state. I can’t tell if these things are connected or not, but it’s really starting to interfere with my job and being present with my wife.
D005-D010_h025.question_a:
I’ve been really off for about three months now. It started with this absolute certainty that something is wrong inside my body. I’m convinced there’s some kind of parasite or device in my abdomen, like something’s burrowed in there and is controlling me. I’ve had scans and blood tests at urgent care and with my GP, but when they say nothing’s there, it just feels like they’re missing it or hiding it.

Around the same time, I began smelling this strong, chemical‑burnt odor, like melted plastic or wiring, especially at night or when I’m at the warehouse. No one else notices it, but to me it’s overpowering, like it’s leaking out of my body.

My wife says I move “weird” now—before I talk I sort of tap my chest twice and straighten my sleeves in this exact way, even during meetings. I know it looks odd, but it feels necessary, like if I don’t, things will go wrong.

For maybe a week or two I felt unusually energized—sleeping 3–4 hours, talking fast, making big plans for restructuring our whole logistics chain. That surge faded, but these beliefs and smells and odd movements have stayed the whole time, every day.
D005-D010_h025.question_b:

Since then I’ve barely slept—maybe two or three hours a night—and I still wake up feeling wired, like I’ve drunk ten coffees. I’m talking nonstop at work and at home, jumping from one idea to another. I’ve been taking on way too many projects at the warehouse, convinced I can reorganize the whole supply chain by myself, and getting irritated when people can’t keep up.

Around the same time this started, I became absolutely convinced something’s wrong inside my chest, like my organs are rotting or rearranging. I keep pressing on my ribs or tapping my sternum in this little pattern before meetings—my wife says it looks odd, but it feels necessary, like it keeps things in place. I also keep smelling this sickly, chemical‑rotting odor that no one else notices, even in clean rooms.

Those smells and the belief about my insides only happen when I’m in this revved‑up state. When I briefly calm down for a day or so, they fade too—but as soon as the high energy and racing thoughts come back, so do they.
